# Generated evidence: safe/remove-owner

Written by `pnpm report safe/remove-owner --record` from `templates/safe/remove-owner/template.json`, `templates/safe/remove-owner/docs.json`, `registry/contracts.json`, `testdata/report/safe-remove-owner.json`, `testdata/abi`. The listings and pages were read on 2026-11-16. `pnpm test` computes it again from these files and fails on any difference: every section is recomputed from the recorded answers except the vault evidence, which is stored as `pnpm vault-evidence` printed it. The recordings were made on the AI's computer; `pnpm report safe/remove-owner --compare` reads the listings, pages, ABI proofs, code spans, ERC-7730 attestations and DefiLlama's protocol entries and hacks live, reads each vault again at the blocks its evidence names and each protocol fact and token's decimals at the block it was read at, fetches each recorded past transaction again by hash, and prints each fact that differs. It does not search for past transactions again, so it cannot show that a search found every one. Text from outside the program appears only as identifiers: a contract name Etherscan gives, printed only when it is a Solidity identifier, and the file paths, field paths and format names `pnpm erc7730` prints. The URLs come from the registry and `docs.json`, in RFC 3986 characters only. Text the AI wrote appears only where a row says it was written by the AI in the template. Do not edit this file.

## Calls and field rules

### Call 1 of 1

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `to` | the Safe |
| `value` | constant `0` |
| `removeOwner` | calls `removeOwner(address,address,uint256)`, selector `0xf8dc5dd9`; no bytes after the arguments |
| `removeOwner.prevOwner` | the owner listed just before the card's `owner` in the Safe's `getOwners()`, read on chain, or the sentinel `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001` when it is first |
| `removeOwner.owner` | the card's `owner` |
| `removeOwner._threshold` | the card's `threshold` |

## Effects

The Safe gives and gets nothing: any change to its balances is a `MISMATCH`.

The Safe's own settings, read just before and just after the transaction: its owners lose exactly the card's `owner`, who must be an owner before, compared as a set; its threshold ends at the card's `threshold`; its singleton, modules, guard and fallback handler stay the same. Any other change is a `MISMATCH`.

## Official documentation

Each page comes from `docs.json`, whose contract must be the one the template calls the function on when the template binds it. The program compares the page's registrable domain, or GitHub organization, with the DefiLlama protocol that contract belongs to, its factory's for an entry a factory deploys, checks that a GitHub page is pinned to a commit on the default branch, and looks in the page as served, without scripts, for the function's name written as code: directly followed by `(`, between backticks, or alone as a block, such as a heading, a list item or a table cell. A PASS there shows that the page names a function of that name, not that it documents this contract's function. A function a token standard defines may instead name that standard: its page, the GitHub org that publishes it and the function's declaration are held by the program, the page must hold that declaration, and its org is compared with the standard's, not with the contract's protocol. Such a PASS shows that the standard defines the function, not that this contract follows the standard.

## Code pins

Every span of each entry's registry code pin, oldest first: a span holds from its block to the block before the next span's. A transaction to sign must run the last span's code, and an executed one the code of the span that holds its block. `pnpm pin-code` writes the spans from the chain, not from a review of that code. Chain: whether, through both providers, the code at the span's first block is its pin, and the code at the block before is the previous span's pin, or for the first span, no code `pnpm pin-code` can pin. A lone pin from block 0 was written before ranges and is not read.

## ABI proofs

`pnpm prove-abi`: Etherscan's verified source, compiled with a pinned solc, against the code both providers return; Etherscan's own ABI is not read. Equals pin: whether the proved code, and the implementation behind a proxy, are the last span of the registry's code pin, which every signing of a new transaction requires. Template functions: whether every function the template calls or reads on the entry, by canonical signature, is in the compiled ABI.
